lessons.title: Meet the cat’s viewpoint
lessons.description: Friends notice the master’s new supplies and the cat’s dry observations.
lessons.canDo: Separate narrator description, inference and the master’s own words.

lessons.title: Read the original painting passage
lessons.description: Follow three consecutive Sōseki paragraphs with supported literary readings.
lessons.canDo: Recover an unanswered question and read 甘く correctly in context.

lessons.title: Keep the voices and the final smile
lessons.description: Track attributed advice and write a summary of what these paragraphs actually show.
lessons.canDo: Preserve contrasting reactions and quotation attribution when summarising.

grammar.title: Recognise a narrator’s written copula
grammar.formation: Noun / na-adjective stem + である; narrative ending だ／である differs from polite です.
grammar.explanation: A written narrator can state a description with である. Identify who is narrating before assuming the statement is a character’s spoken line. In this passage おらん retrieves the older negative from unit 3.

examples.ja: {吾輩|わがはい}は{猫|ねこ}である。
これは{主人|しゅじん}の{述懐|じゅっかい}である。
この{本|ほん}は{短編|たんぺん}ではなく、{長編|ちょうへん}である。
examples.en: This book is a long work, not a short one.

grammar.mistake: である is a written style choice here, not a more polite way to address a friend. Noun + である; do not insert だ before it.

grammar.title: Separate an observed action from とみえる
grammar.formation: Plain verb / i-adjective clause + とみえる／と見えた; the clause describes an inference from available signs.
grammar.explanation: The narrator sees the new art materials and infers a decision to paint. The next day’s painting is a separate observed action. The wording suggests a conclusion; it does not quote a decision the master told the cat. The source itself uses the shorter nominal phrase 決心と見えた; the practice examples use complete plain verb/adjective clauses.
grammar.example: 道具を買った。絵をかくことにしたと見えた。
grammar.translation: He bought the tools. It seemed he had decided to paint.

examples.ja: {道具|どうぐ}を{買|か}った。{絵|え}をかくことにしたと{見|み}えた。
examples.en: He bought the tools. It seemed he had decided to paint.

examples.ja: {電気|でんき}が{消|き}えている。もう{帰|かえ}ったとみえる。
examples.en: The lights are off. It looks as though they have already gone home.

examples.ja: {窓|まど}を{開|あ}けた。{部屋|へや}が{暑|あつ}いとみえる。
examples.en: She opened the window. It seems the room is hot.

grammar.mistake: Keep the observation and inferred conclusion separate. In this taught pattern とみえる is not a report that somebody said the words aloud.

grammar.title: Recover the unanswered question in やら
grammar.formation: Question-word clause in plain form + やら; selected literary uncertainty here, not the AやらBやら list pattern.
grammar.explanation: 何をかいたものやら leaves the picture’s subject unclear. Recover the embedded question as 何をかいたのか. The negative 誰にも鑑定がつかない answers the larger context: nobody can identify it.
grammar.example: 何をかいたものやら、誰にも分からない。
grammar.translation: Nobody can tell what he has drawn.

examples.ja: {何|なに}をかいたものやら、{誰|だれ}にも{分|わ}からない。
examples.en: Nobody can tell what he has drawn.

examples.ja: いつ{帰|かえ}るやら、まだ{分|わ}からない。
examples.en: I still don’t know when he’ll come back.

examples.ja: この{話|はなし}はどう{終|お}わるやら。
examples.en: I wonder how this story will end.

grammar.mistake: A question-word + やら clause expresses uncertainty here. Do not translate it as a completed identification or teach every やら as a list.

grammar.title: Follow the speaker inside a quotation
grammar.formation: Quoted clause + と + 言う／答える; nested quotation can introduce another attributed speaker.
grammar.explanation: The friend says that an artist gave advice; the master then responds to that claim. Track each reporting voice. The source lets you identify who attributes the words, rather than proving the quoted art-history claim.
grammar.example: 友人は「自然を写せ」と言った。

examples.ja: {友人|ゆうじん}は「{自然|しぜん}を{写|うつ}せ」と{言|い}った。
{先生|せんせい}は、{友人|ゆうじん}がそう{言|い}ったと{説明|せつめい}した。
examples.en: The teacher explained that the friend had said that.

examples.ja: {主人|しゅじん}は「{知|し}らなかった」と{答|こた}えた。
examples.en: The master replied, “I didn’t know that.”

grammar.mistake: Read the words after the closing quotation mark as well. Otherwise the friend’s attributed advice can be mistaken for something the narrator personally asserts.

dialogues.title: Art supplies after work
dialogues.description: Friends compare the cat’s observation with their own unfinished hobbies.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: {主人|しゅじん}は{少|すく}なくとも{筆|ふで}を{持|も}ってるよ。
lines.romaji: Shujin wa sukunakutomo fude o motteru yo.
lines.meaning: At least the master actually picks up the brush.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {猫|ねこ}よりハナの{方|ほう}が{優|やさ}しいな。
lines.romaji: Neko yori Hana no hō ga yasashii na.
lines.meaning: Hana’s kinder than the cat.

dialogues.title: Who is speaking on this line?
dialogues.description: Satō-sensei helps Bao read the disputed word and follow the voices.

lines.speaker: You

recycling.reason: The cat-reading rehearsal naturally retrieves unit 7’s 言い回し: Ren practices the actual 吾輩 expression assigned to him. Painting and literature headwords belong in recognition menus; the friends’ conversation is not padded with administrative words.
